title: Timestamp Problems occured  when Upgraded to 2.1.2
body:
hello,

Some logs were stopped after upgrading to 2.1.2 I noticed that my "Trino" logs stream was stopped after upgrading and there was no error or warning. After opening stdout, I observed the difference.

My logs was like that before upgrading below.

[ 23423423.423424, { ....... } ]

Then after upgrading to 2.2.1 below.

[ [0.00000000 , {} ] ,  { ....... } ]

I could not understand why? 

thanks

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Could you share your configuration file and some more context? Otherwise there isn't much we can say about it.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
It seems like it could be a problem in `filter_parser` and I wonder if it's the same one fixed by [this PR](https://github.com/fluent/fluent-bit/pull/7323) but the only way I can think of testing it would be running the nightly container or building from master.

Do you think you'd be able to do it?
A different yet somewhat noisier approach would be interleaving these blocks between your current filter blocks and after the last one which would cause fluent-bit to print the records to its log file (or stdout) as they flow through the system : 

```
      [FILTER]
          Name          stdout
          Match         kube.my_svc.*
```

Obviously this last approach is not something you would put in a production environment but it could be a pretty valuable source of information.

Would you be able to share a sample input file with me (you could send it in private through slack if you prefer it that way) so I can look into it?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: We needed a feature from 2.1.2 so we did not want to downgrade, so for a workaround, set Current_Time_Index = On In this way logs can stream to the right index file. We are storing them as daily log files. The log files streamed to "index_0.0.0" because of this bug. But Current_Time_Index solved index name problems.
